NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice tracks spindle temperature at discrete points using embedded thermocouples. My observable is the thermal gradient along the spindle shaft length, calculated from existing temperature sensors, which provides an early warning of thermal deformation before significant tool center point displacement occurs. This departure matters because thermal gradient drives differential expansion, which is the direct cause of shaft bending and tool center point shift.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: ΔL = α × L × ΔT, where thermal expansion (ΔL) is proportional to the coefficient of thermal expansion (α), length (L), and temperature change (ΔT). For steel spindle (α ≈ 11×10⁻⁶ /°C), a 1°C gradient over 200mm length produces ΔL = 2.2 micrometers. This magnitude is significant relative to the 10μm constraint, confirming thermal gradient as a meaningful leading indicator.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components: 1) Existing spindle thermocouples (minimum 3, axially distributed), 2) Data acquisition system (already installed), 3) Processing unit (PLC or controller with math capabilities). Materials: None required beyond existing infrastructure. Procedure: Calculate temperature difference between axial thermocouples using standard subtraction. Compute thermal gradient as (T_top - T_bottom) / distance_between_sensors. Implementation requires only software modification to existing control system - no hardware changes.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors
- Operability: SAME - no additional operator interface required
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance points
- Cost class: SAME - only software development cost
- Data processing: MINOR increase (gradient calculation) but well within existing controller capability
Conclusion: Deployment burden is equivalent to standard practice while providing earlier warning of thermal deformation.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: 1) Cold start spindle at 20°C ambient, 2) Record temperature readings at 1-second intervals, 3) Calculate thermal gradient between top and bottom thermocouples, 4) Measure tool center point displacement via laser interferometer, 5) Repeat for 3 warmup cycles.
Instruments: Existing spindle thermocouples, laser interferometer, data logger.
Pass threshold: Thermal gradient remains below 0.5°C/cm throughout 20-minute warmup, with tool center point displacement <10μm.
Fail criterion: Thermal gradient exceeds 0.5°C/cm at any point OR tool center point displacement exceeds 10μm at any point.
Duration: 20 minutes per cycle × 3 cycles = 60 minutes total.
Kill criterion: Immediate termination if tool center point displacement exceeds 10μm at any point.
